proposed_comments.title: Keep Win-key hold separate from the activation hotkey
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep Win-key hold separate from the activation hotkey

**Severity:** `high`

The new `OpenShortcutGuide` branch infers a Windows-key hold from `GetAsyncKeyState` inside an asynchronously queued UI callback, while the activation hotkey and the Win-key hold both signal the same Shortcut Guide event. A Win-containing activation hotkey such as the default Win+Shift+/ can therefore be routed through the Windows-key action path: with `Off` it can be dropped, with `TaskbarIndicators` it can open the wrong pane, and when the overlay is already visible the new `OpenShortcutGuide` branch returns instead of using the normal toggle-close path.

Please carry the trigger source explicitly from the runner/module interface to the Shortcut Guide process, for example by using a distinct Win-key-hold event/message and keeping the existing trigger event for the regular activation hotkey. In the Win-key `OpenShortcutGuide` path, also refresh `Program.ForegroundWindowHandle` before calling `MainPaneControl.Open()` so app-specific shortcuts are resolved against the current foreground app.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve settings telemetry and the configured hold delay
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve settings telemetry and the configured hold delay

**Severity:** `high`

`send_settings_telemetry()` now calls `EnsureProcessRuns("telemetry")`, but the helper returns early whenever the persistent Shortcut Guide UI process is already running. `Program.Main` only emits the settings telemetry event when a process is actually launched with the `telemetry` argument, so settings telemetry becomes a no-op in the common enabled case.

Please keep telemetry as a transient launch path that does not reuse or replace the tracked UI-process handle and does not reset pending UI trigger events. This change should also restore the `press_time` parsing/clamping and return `m_millisecondsWinKeyPressTimeForGlobalWindowsShortcuts` instead of hard-coding 900 ms, otherwise the Settings `PressTime` value from 100-5000 ms no longer affects Win-key hold activation.
